title: Redwood All-Hands - December 2026
summary: Monthly company all-hands. Q&A included pricing, Dedicated capacity SLAs, and a short demo of the new observability dashboard. Meeting ended with clear next steps and action owners.

transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-12-08 | Start: 10:00 PST | Duration: ~62 mins | Location: All-hands virtual
Attendees: Samara Liu (CEO), Ben Carter (CTO), Leah Kim (VP Eng), Ravi Desai (Head of Product), Maya Chen (Head of People), Samir Patel (Head of Revenue) + company-wide

Summary: Samara opened with a short state of the company message, highlighted traction in Dedicated and Private deals, and thanked teams for hitting Q4 targets. Ben went into some technical wins — latency reductions from kernel selection improvements and batching, and an update on Private deployment networking patterns. Ravi walked through the Q1 roadmap priorities and the Redwood Optimize pilot. People announced two leadership hires and some role restructures. The session ended with a live 6-minute demo of the new Observability dashboard and a Q&A.

00:00 Samara Liu: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick housekeeping, recording is on. Big thank you for Q4 effort, we beat our net new ARR target and that's thanks to a lot of the work across infra and product. Um, quick note on customer momentum, Dedicated deals are up—up by, hmm, about 35% quarter over quarter, and Private pilots are ramping.

00:32 Samara Liu: I want to call out the SE and solutions folks who ran the NVIDIA benchmark last month, that fed directly into our datapoint with, with the retail customer, so really appreciate that. We'll post the benchmark sheet in the #announcements channel.

01:05 Ben Carter: Thanks Samara, on the eng side we've been focused on kernel selection improvements — that's, uh, picking the best kernels per layer and per sequence length distribution — leading to about a 12 to 18% inference latency improvement on average in our internal tests. There's also continuous batching gains; with smarter prefix caching we saw token cost reductions. Note: some of the numbers are POC-level, still needs broader validation.

01:40 Ben Carter: Private deployment update: we've improved the VPC onboarding flow, and the compatibility matrix will list supported KMS providers and allowed CIDR patterns. There's still a tricky edge case with some on-prem firewalls that requires manual routing — we'll document the workaround.

02:12 Ravi Desai: On product for Q1, top priorities: 1) Redwood Optimize — roll out pilot for cost-aware profiles, 2) Observability 2.0 — per-route token cost breakdowns and alerting, 3) model lifecycle tooling — easier pinning and canary rollouts. We'll be prioritizing pilot customers for Optimize and starting trials in January.

02:45 Leah Kim: On reliability, we've been tuning autoscaling for Dedicated pools; there were incidents mid-November tied to a scheduler bug — we've patched and added an extra canary stage. SLA metrics look stable now but we'll keep monitoring.

03:10 Maya Chen: Hiring update: two leaders joining — Heads of Customer Success and Security — both start mid-January. We're also opening roles in infra and solutions engineering; org chart will be posted. Please refer to the hiring doc for interview rubrics.

03:35 Samir Patel: Quick GTM update — PLG motion continues to be effective, onboarding time reduced by half for API-first customers. For enterprise, we're pushing more named accounts into Dedicated, and pricing questions about committed vs. usage continue to come up — we'll update the FAQ.

04:00 Audience Q&A (typed):
04:05 Anonymous: Any news on SOC 2 / ISO efforts?
04:08 Maya Chen: We're progressing on SOC 2 Type II — audit kickoff next week; ISO timeline is Q2. Will share the schedule in #security channel.

04:24 Anonymous: For Private deployments, what's the expected lead time?
04:28 Ben Carter: Typical lead time for VPC-based Private is 2–4 weeks depending on network approvals, on-prem is longer and depends on customer infra. We'll share the compatibility matrix for faster evaluation.

04:45 Anonymous: Are we seeing model quality regressions with quantized variants?
04:48 Ravi Desai: Good question; we run quality regressions tied to prompt suites — current regressions are low but it's model dependent. Redwood Optimize will include recommended quantization profiles per workload.

05:10 (Demo) Ravi Desai: — switching screens — here's Observability 2.0, main dashboard shows per-route latency, token cost, and ribbons for model version. You can break down by token type and see a trace for a single request. Note: demo data is synthetic.

05:45 Ben Carter: There was a live example of a canary rollback on the dashboard — you can see automatic fallback to a cheaper variant when latency spikes, that's the graceful degradation flow.

06:10 Samara Liu: Ok final few items — roadmap cadence will shift to monthly leadership reviews and quarterly company OKR checkpoints. We want tighter telemetry around customer unit economics.

06:30 Samir Patel: Recap of next steps: I'll share the Q4 deck; Ben will publish the Private compatibility matrix; Ravi opens the Optimize RFC; Maya posts hiring plan. Also, pricing FAQ update for GTM. Everyone, if you have questions, ping the respective leads.

06:52 Samara Liu: Thank you everyone, happy holidays, enjoy the rest of your week. Meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcript quality: brief run-ons, some technical terms abbreviated and occasionally mis-transcribed (e.g., VPC pronounced V-P-C, KV cache sometimes transcribed as K-V cash).
